display_title: Trump Rules Out Iran Attack Before Midterms
display_title_he: טראמפ פוסל תקיפה באיראן לפני בחירות האמצע
short_summary: President Donald Trump announced that the U.S. will not launch military strikes against Iran before the November 3 midterm elections, citing ongoing discussions and a desire to manage domestic political fallout.

image.credit: Alisdare Hickson from Canterbury, United Kingdom · CC BY-SA 2.0

sources.name: CNBC
sources.title: Trump says U.S. will not attack Iran before midterm election

sources.name: JNS
sources.title: No renewed attack on Iran before Election Day, Trump says

paragraphs: In a striking alignment of foreign policy and domestic political calculations, President Donald Trump announced that the United States will refrain from launching any military strikes against Iran prior to the upcoming midterm elections on November 3. Writing on his social media platform, Truth Social, Trump explicitly tied the timing of potential military escalation to the American electoral calendar, declaring that no offensive actions would occur before voters head to the polls. He added that the administration is currently engaged in "productive discussions" with Tehran.

This announcement represents a swift rhetorical pivot. Only a day earlier, Trump had signaled to reporters that renewed strikes were under active consideration, a warning that immediately rattled global energy markets. Following those comments, Brent crude surged over four percent, climbing past $104 a barrel. Despite his more diplomatic tone on Thursday, Trump emphasized that the stringent U.S. naval blockade of Iran would remain fully active, reiterating his administration's stance that Tehran will never be permitted to acquire a nuclear weapon.

The strategic pause comes amid mounting domestic pressure and shifting public sentiment. According to a Reuters/Ipsos poll from August, American public support for military action against Iran has dwindled to just 31 percent, down from 37 percent in March. Furthermore, an overwhelming 83 percent of respondents expressed concern that the conflict would drag on indefinitely.

For the Republican Party, the electoral stakes are exceptionally high. The conflict has exacerbated inflation, driving fuel costs up and leaving GOP candidates vulnerable on the critical issue of affordability. According to AAA data, national average gas prices have soared to $4.36 a gallon—a roughly 40 percent increase from a year ago, and a sharp rise from the $2.98 average recorded just before the outbreak of hostilities in late February. Consequently, high energy prices have become a central theme in Democratic campaign advertisements, prompting several Republican candidates in highly competitive congressional races to publicly distance themselves from the president's war policy.

Behind closed doors, the political calendar has heavily influenced White House strategy. Reports indicate that senior aides have actively lobbied to contain the conflict until after the midterms to mitigate electoral losses, while keeping the option of heavier strikes on the table once the ballots are cast. Meanwhile, a substantial military buildup continues in the Middle East. The United States is deploying approximately 9,000 sailors and Marines alongside a third aircraft carrier to the region, a move that could place three American carrier strike groups in the area by late October.

Diplomatic channels also remain open. Qatar has been mediating negotiations between Washington and Tehran, which began during the United Nations General Assembly in September. While Trump maintains that Iran's economy and military are in "very bad condition," he expressed optimism that Tehran would agree to a comprehensive deal shortly after Election Day. However, the economic toll of the standoff remains severe. Senator Chris Murphy noted that daily liquefied natural gas shipments through the vital Strait of Hormuz have plummeted from ten tankers before the war to just one or two today, while maritime insurance costs have skyrocketed from $100,000 to over $1 million per day.

Trump stated that the U.S. is currently engaged in productive discussions with Tehran.
